regime_context: As-of 2026-10-30 the detector is in a narrowing, non-one-narrative regime: 22 of 49 themes are trend-eligible (absolute-trend gate open, gate_helps=true), but the rotation leader (Memory/HBM, score 2.31) is NOT eligible while the secondary leader (US Energy Complex, eligible, score 1.42) is crowded. Rotation margin is wide (0.89) and absorption is low (0.31), so no confirmed handoff — leadership concentration is display-only, not a forecast.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Memory/HBM (rotation leader, score 2.31, rank 1) breaks HIGHER into trend eligibility — it currently fails the absolute-trend gate (eligible=false, durability_bar=0.30) and has breadth 0.0. The observable that retires this watch: eligibility flips to true AND breadth rises above 0.5, i.e. the leader turns into a broad, gate-approved trend rather than a narrow outlier.

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: The trend-gate leg (the only validated edge here) is open for Energy Complex (eligible=true) with strong breadth (0.955) and mixed-but-non-failing Hurst, so it survives the drawdown/shake-out filter. Its high score and crowd flag (crowded=true) are coincident attention/focus signals — NOT return forecasts — so this is a continuation-with-discipline lean: stay exposed via the gate, but do not size up on the crowding flag.
theses.dissent: XLE is energy-complex and already crowded (z=1.03); the gate says nothing about future return, and equal-weight energy (same XLE proxy) could stay flat while large-cap energy rolls over, giving a false sense of leadership.

falsifier.text: XLE closes below its 20-day trend filter (absolute-trend gate flips to ineligible) before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is trend-eligible with the second-highest durability_bar (0.79) and high breadth (0.889), passing the validated drawdown gate. Its crowding_z=1.68 is a size-down caution only, not a reason to avoid; a low-conviction overweight respects the only leg with an edge (trend-gate staying power).
theses.dissent: PPH is a concentrated large-cap pharma proxy — the trend may be a defensive-macro artifact rather than sector strength, and crowding of 1.68 is the most extended of the eligible leaders.

falsifier.text: PPH underperforms SPY by 5% over the horizon and breadth (as measured by constituents above their own trend filters) falls below 0.6

theses.subject: Utilities (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Utilities (EW) has strong breadth (0.871) and a negative crowding_z (-0.21, uncrowded), but it FAILS the absolute-trend gate (eligible=false, durability_bar only 0.51). Since the gate is the one validated leg here, an ineligible theme gets no exposure call beyond avoidance — despite the decent appearance of the other coincident metrics.
evidence: breadth=0.871, crowding_z=-0.21 (uncrowded but irrelevant to eligibility)
theses.dissent: XLU breadth is genuinely strong and uncrowded; if macro conditions push defensives, this could mean-revert higher while the gate lag keeps it excluded.

falsifier.text: XLU flips to eligible=true on a durable rise before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
